statements.text: We can't afford to let China win the data and AI or artificial intelligence race. That said, if we're going to have a data center, I think that there are certain conditions that should apply,
statements.venue: KETV report on Iowa 4th District race

statements.text: The reality is that AI is an incredible technology. Let's call it what it is. It's revolutionary. But we do recognize that there are many people that are advocating for kill switches. [...] I'll wrap up my answer by also saying we are in a technology race over AI with the Chinese. We have to make sure we lead the world in artificial intelligence but we do have guardrails.
statements.venue: Iowa 4th District candidate debate, reported by Sioux City Journal/The Gazette

statements.text: I have said on numerous occasions that there is a role for the federal government in policing AI, and I know that puts me in a disagreement with the current administration, but I stand by that. We have to protect citizens. Now, AI is coming, and I don't want to say that we should stop or slow down because we're involved in an arms race on AI with the Chinese, and we must prevail in this.
statements.venue: Iowa PBS Iowa Press debate, 4th Congressional District

statements.text: If we're going to continue to have an insatiable appetite for data, we're going to have AI, and we're going to have data centers. But I do believe there is a role for the federal government in policing and protecting us.
statements.venue: Iowa PBS Iowa Press debate, 4th Congressional District

statements.text: I do think there’s a need for some guardrails, and I don’t believe that we can defer all that to the private sector,
